subject: physics_2
question_text: What is an n-type semiconductor? What are the majority and minority charge carriers in it.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the space before the first question mark is dropped. The book writes 'N-type'; the standard lowercase 'n-type' is used here, and named donor examples (P, As, Sb) are added — the book gives none.

recall_prompt: Say what is added to make an n-type semiconductor, and name its majority and minority carriers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: n-type semiconductor
lines: impurity is added to a pure semiconductor,
the result is an n-type semiconductor.
arsenic and antimony. They are called
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word pentavalent carries it; the named examples are a bonus.
steps.why: A pentavalent atom has five valence electrons but only four are needed for the bonds with the neighbouring silicon atoms. The fifth is left loosely held and becomes a free electron, so the crystal gains electrons without gaining charge.
common_mistakes: Saying trivalent. Trivalent doping gives p-type.
Saying the crystal becomes negatively charged. It stays neutral — each donor atom keeps its positive ion behind.

recall.must_convey: That adding a pentavalent (donor) impurity to a pure semiconductor gives an n-type semiconductor.
accept: five valence electrons added to silicon

steps.memory_tip: n for negative, and pentavalent gives the spare electron.

steps.label: Majority and minority
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both carriers must be named; naming one is half the answer.
steps.why: Doping adds electrons only. The few holes present come from thermal breaking of covalent bonds, which happens in any semiconductor, so they are far fewer than the donated electrons and are the minority.
common_mistakes: Saying there are no holes at all in n-type. There are a few, produced by heat.
Swapping the two. In n-type the electrons are the majority.

recall.must_convey: That electrons are the majority carriers and holes the minority carriers in n-type.

steps.memory_tip: n-type = negative carriers in the majority.

insider_note: Both carriers must be named for the second mark. Writing only 'electrons' earns only half of it.
